rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A detailed study of Dryopteris (fern) shows a short, creeping, scaled rhizome bearing adventitious roots and fronds. The frond (stipe + blade) has pinnae and pinules, with sori (clusters of sporangia with an annulus and indusium) on the underside. Meiosis in the spore mother cell produces spores that germinate into the small, heart-shaped prothallus (gametophyte), which bears antheridia and archegonia.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Frond: stipe + blade (pinnae + pinules) + sori (indusium-covered)
Sporangium: annulus + meiosis → spores (n)
Prothallus: heart-shaped; antheridia + archegonia; sperm (2 flagella) + egg

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The prothallus (gametophyte) is small and heart-shaped; it is NOT the main plant body (that is the frond-bearing sporophyte).  ·  Sori are clusters of sporangia on the frond underside; the indusium covers them (not the sori themselves).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a detailed Dryopteris frond diagram (stipe, blade, pinnae, sori, indusium, annulus).  ·  The sorus structure (sporangium + annulus + indusium) is a very common exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Dryopteris frond: stipe + blade; pinnae + pinules; sori on the underside with indusium.  ·  Rhizome: short, creeping, scaled, with adventitious roots.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The annulus is the specialized dehiscent structure of the sporangium (a row of cells that snaps the capsule open).  ·  Fertilisation STILL requires water in pteridophytes (flagellated sperm) — a key exam point.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Dryopteris frond: stipe + blade; pinnae + pinules; sori on the underside.  ·  Sorus: cluster of sporangia; annulus (dehiscent) + indusium (cover).  ·  Prothallus: small, heart-shaped, free-living; antheridia + archegonia.  ·  Fertilisation requires water (flagellated sperm).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Ferns first appeared in the Carboniferous (~300 Ma); their fossils form coal.  ·  The Dryopteris frond is the standard NEB model fern.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: DETAILED PTERIDOPHYTE (Dryopteris) MORPHOLOGY AND REPRODUCTION.  ·  Rhizome: short, creeping, bearing scales + adventitious roots; the main vegetative organ.  ·  Frond: the leaf-like organ; stipe (stalk) + blade (lamina); blade divided into pinnae, each into pinules.
